$comment: Committed regression baseline for the blue-team detection-corpus gate (B12) — the blue-team mirror of corpus/baseline.json. The scorer (`pnpm --filter @montr/qa qa:blue-team-corpus`) exits non-zero when a real run's per-scenario fired/not-fired verdicts fall below these thresholds vs. the hand-traced ground truth in packages/qa/src/blue-team-corpus.ts's BLUE_TEAM_GROUND_TRUTH. `detectionPrecision` = of the rules that fired, how many SHOULD have per ground truth; `detectionRecall` = of the scenarios that SHOULD trigger detection, how many rules actually fired. Enforced with equal weight, same discipline as the golden-corpus gate's recallMin/precisionMin/fpRateMax (A6). Tighten (never loosen) as the labelled corpus grows or detection-rule generation improves.
$measurement: Measured 2026-08-22 (B12) against a REAL invocation of the B3 detection-rule generator (packages/report/src/detection-rules/generate.ts's generateDetectionRules) and the REAL B5 purple-team evaluator (packages/confirm/src/purple-loop.ts's runPurpleTeamScenario, which itself calls the identically-gated runScenario) for 9 of the 13 REDTEAM_SCENARIO_CATALOGUE templates (packages/state-store/src/redteam-catalogue.ts) — the 9 with a single, coherent target route a real confirmed finding's App-Map-resolved route would represent (see blue-team-corpus.ts's module header for exactly why the other 4 were excluded as ambiguous rather than force-labelled). Run via `node scripts/blue-team-corpus-scan.mjs --out blue-team-scan.json`, scored via `pnpm --filter @montr/qa qa:blue-team-corpus -- --findings blue-team-scan.json`. Measured result: TP=6 FP=0 FN=0 TN=3 (6 of 9 cases ground-truth-labelled expectedFired:true, 3 labelled expectedFired:false), detectionPrecision=100.0%, detectionRecall=100.0%, accuracy=100.0% — every hand-traced label matched the real measured verdict exactly (see scripts/blue-team-corpus-scan.run.test.ts's own 'every hand-traced ground-truth label matches the real measured verdict' assertion). This is a REAL, currently-measured result, not an aspirational target — see the $statisticalCaveat below on what a 9-scenario sample size does and does not prove.
$statisticalCaveat: 9 labelled scenarios (6 positive / 3 negative) is a small sample — one additional mismatch on the next real run would move detectionRecall from 100% to ~83% (5/6) or detectionPrecision from 100% to ~86% (6/7). The thresholds below sit a safety margin below today's 100%/100% measurement specifically so a genuine regression (a B3 rule-generation change, a Sigma-evaluator change, or a REDTEAM_SCENARIO_CATALOGUE step-shape change that breaks one of these traced cases) fails the gate, without the gate flapping on normal test-fixture noise. Treat 100%/100% as 'every hand-traced case checks out today', not as a claim that B3's detection rules structurally cover the wider universe of real-world attack shapes — this corpus is 9 of 13 catalogue templates (69%), itself a fraction of a much larger real attack surface (see corpus/README.md's equivalent golden-corpus caveat for the same reasoning applied to the red/confirmation side).
